chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf, so he said: 'Their time is when you have finished your Tawaf, and I dislike them when the sun is yellowing (at sunset) and when it is rising.'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf prayer

ai.seo_question: When is the best time to pray the two rak'ahs of Tawaf?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the two rak'ahs of Tawaf are ideally performed immediately after completing the circumambulation, they are disliked (makruh) during the specific times of sunrise (ishraq) and sunset (ghurub). This ruling reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential principle of avoiding voluntary prayers during these transitional solar moments to distinguish them from the sun's own worship, ensuring the ritual remains focused on the Kaaba.
